what_i_did: Listed 349 visible features region by region before modelling; each is a named object or a justified merge (48 merges).
Counted rail lugs in the right photo (0.897 px/mm) and wrote every outline in that photo's pixels, so each number can be checked against the image.
301 named parts under HK416 > upper, lower, handguard, barrel_assembly, stock, grip, magazine, sights, controls, fasteners, with 7 game sockets.
Moving parts run in real cavities (bolt carrier bore, charging handle channel, magazine well, button pocket, bolt catch relief), so the clips do not pass through solid metal.
Three procedural materials (anodized aluminium, glass-filled polymer, phosphate steel) baked with Cycles to 2048 px base colour, occlusion-roughness-metallic and normal sets, embedded in the GLB.
Silhouette IoU, assembly, animation overlap, inventory coverage and GLB reload are scripts in tools/, rerun every round.
good: Right-photo silhouette IoU 0.968 at a fixed scale with no fitting.
No floating parts; every clip stays under 0.2 mm of overlap.
Barrel measures 14.5 in in the reloaded GLB.
ADS view through the ghost ring lines up with the front post.
off: Drawing silhouettes are below the 0.92 target: the drawing shows a short-barrel rifle with a longer handguard, and its rail is not drawn to MIL-STD pitch. The photo itself scores about the same against the drawing as the model does. One model cannot score 0.92 on the photo and on the drawing.
Rear sight: the photo shows a bulky diopter-style sight; the model's folding arm is slimmer and its windage knob sits elsewhere (the largest remaining silhouette mismatch, about 260 px of 53,845).
Handguard length: the model follows the photo (9.0 in, 19 lugs per rail). Not confirmed against an independent source for the D14.5RS.
No rail slot numbers, no maker marks, no words on the selector (pictograms only).
Lateral sizes are AR-pattern values, not measured: no top or front reference was supplied.
The upper receiver is a clean extrusion with added parts; the real forging's scallops around the forward assist and the cam-pin bulge are simplified.
Stock and grip are slab-sided lofts with rounded edges; the real mouldings have more compound curvature and a thinner lower strut.
The magazine follows the photo's wide, strongly ribbed magazine (the .22 LR pattern), not a STANAG steel magazine.
Mould seams, the selector lever's grooves and the receivers' cast texture exist only as normal-map grain.
Ambient occlusion is baked at the rest pose (magazine moved out of the well for the bake); the bolt carrier and the stock's bore stay dark when they move.

moving_parts: 13 glTF clips at 24 fps: charge (30 frames), dust_cover_open (10 frames), mag_release (10 frames), mag_out (24 frames), mag_in (22 frames), bolt_catch (12 frames), safety_to_fire (6 frames), safety_to_safe (6 frames), trigger_pull (10 frames), stock_extend (46 frames), stock_collapse (46 frames), sights_down (8 frames), sights_up (8 frames). Each moving part has its origin on its hinge or slide axis. stock_extend and stock_collapse stop at each of the six positions (0, 15, 30, 45, 60, 75 mm) for four frames.
creative_additions: Three-position fire-control pictograms (safe, single, automatic) with no words; two cartridges in the magazine for reload; a first-person hip render. No maker marks, no orange.
